Living Well / Free resources

Free learning & practical understanding

A useful way in

Choose one place to begin.

Build a little understanding through open lessons, course materials, textbooks, and visual demonstrations.

You can learn one useful thing without enrolling in a complete program. Choose a question you would like to answer, then match the resource to the size of that question. A plain tutorial may be more useful today than a university lecture series, while a textbook can provide a reference to return to.

Start with: LearnFree: everyday skills. Choose one tutorial that matches a task you actually need to do.

Khan Academy

Khan Academy

Open textbooks · Free to browse

OpenStax textbooks

OpenStax, Rice University

A stable reference for checking an explanation against a fuller account instead of relying only on a generated answer.

Begin here: Choose a subject and read the relevant introductory section before tackling exercises.

Access: Digital textbooks are free to read or download. Printed copies and some additional services cost money.

Perspective: University-based open education

PhET interactive simulations

University of Colorado Boulder

A useful way to explore a scientific or mathematical relationship by changing one thing and observing a model.

Begin here: Choose an introductory simulation and predict a change before moving a control.

Access: Free simulations; browser compatibility varies. Some educator features require an account.

Keep the context

Take what is useful, thoughtfully.

Open materials are not automatically current in every detail, and access to a course is not the same as enrollment for academic credit. Check the level, date, and any account requirements. After reading, explain one idea in your own words or try one low-stakes example before moving on.

Selections are based on public source review, not a claim that Nolan uses every resource or belongs to the organizations listed.
